10 levels of the Dasha mahavidya game

The Dasha Mahavidya (Ten Great Wisdom Goddesses) can be conceptualized as a spiritual action-adventure game focusing on the evolution of consciousness, where each goddess represents a level, a challenge, and a "power-up" (siddhi) to overcome the ego. The game takes the player from the destruction of the lower self to ultimate liberation. [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]  


Here is a 10-level game structure based on the Dasha Mahavidya: 

Level 1: Kali (The Destroyer of Time & Ego) 

• Theme: Confrontation with mortality and the end of illusion. 
• Challenge: The player must face their darkest fears and destroy the ego (demon Raktabija). 
• Power-up: Utter fearlessness and the ability to exist beyond time. [8, 9]  

Level 2: Tara (The Saviour & Guide) 

• Theme: Navigating the void and chaos. 
• Challenge: The player is trapped in the middle of an ocean of existence and must find the "inner guide" to escape. 
• Power-up: Ultimate knowledge (Neel Saraswati) and spiritual protection. [1, 10, 11]  

Level 3: Tripura Sundari/Shodashi (The Ruler of Desire) 

• Theme: Perfecting beauty, harmony, and consciousness. 
• Challenge: The player must balance spiritual aspirations with worldly responsibilities, learning to find beauty in all three worlds. 
• Power-up: Mastery over bliss, abundance, and the ability to manifest desires. [14, 15, 16, 17]  

Level 4: Bhuvaneshvari (The World Mother) 

• Theme: Expansion of consciousness. 
• Challenge: The player must perceive the entire universe within their own body, breaking down boundaries of "self" vs. "world". 
• Power-up: Cosmic perspective and control over natural forces. [1, 10, 19]  

Level 5: Bhairavi (The Fierce Goddess of Tapas) 

• Theme: Purifying fire and discipline. 
• Challenge: The player must endure intense self-discipline (tapas) to burn away ignorance and negative habits. 
• Power-up: Inner strength, courage, and the mastery of Kundalini energy. [16, 21, 22]  

Level 6: Chhinnamasta (The Self-Decapitated One) 

• Theme: Radical self-sacrifice and surrender. 
• Challenge: The player must sever their own head (representing the ego) to feed their inner consciousness, demonstrating total detachment. 
• Power-up: Ultimate detachment, transcending mind-based limitations. [15, 24, 25]  

Level 7: Dhumavati (The Widow Goddess) 

• Theme: Embracing the void, scarcity, and inauspiciousness. 
• Challenge: The player must find wisdom in failure, loneliness, and loss. 
• Power-up: Freedom from attachment to "success" and the ability to see the truth behind appearances. [14, 27, 28, 29]  

Level 8: Bagalamukhi (The Paralyzer of Enemies) 

• Theme: Silence and stillness. 
• Challenge: The player must freeze all internal and external distractions (the enemies of speech and mind). 
• Power-up: The ability to paralyze opposing forces and achieve victory through silence. [1, 24, 27]  

Level 9: Matangi (The Tantric Saraswati) 

• Theme: Expression of pure knowledge. 
• Challenge: The player must embrace the unconventional to find the inner truth (raw authenticity) and master speech/arts. 
• Power-up: Mastery over the arts, knowledge, and eloquent speech. [3, 16, 27, 33, 34]  

Level 10: Kamala (The Lotus Goddess) 

• Theme: Absolute prosperity and grace. 
• Challenge: The final step: enjoying the world while remaining unattached to it, fully blooming like a lotus. 
• Power-up: Realization of the Goddess within—total abundance, beauty, and liberation. [1, 16, 27, 35]  

Game Mechanics: 

• Sadhana (Action): The player must maintain intense focus (mantra/yantra) to pass levels. 

• Guidance: A "Guru" is required to navigate the perilous levels. 

• Objective: To move from the bondage of the material world to the freedom of the divine. [2, 36, 37, 38]

Album of popular prints mounted on cloth pages. Colour lithograph, lettered, inscribed and numbered 37. The print is subdivided into ten equal parts, each representing one of the ten aspects of Devi, the divine mother. Each image is identified with a Bengali inscription, and the goddesses represented are: Kali, Tara, Shodashi, Bhuvaneshvari, Bhairavi, Chhinnamasta, Dhumavati, Bagalamukhi, Matangi, and Kamala.
